citedSourceUnits.zh: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！
citedSourceUnits.en: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received appointment as one of the former emperor’s generals. With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!
citedSourceUnits.literal: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received the former emperor's appointment among the generals; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow powerful enemies; therefore from recent times until now, crossing weapons and meeting blades, one season for farming and three for war, yet the troops are not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy fears us more each day and our territory grows daily; how much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 自秦、漢以來，隆赫之極，豈有若此者乎！
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Since Qin and Han, has splendor reached such a height!
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Since Qin and Han, has there been such extreme splendor!

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 以吾觀之，若功就事舉，必享申伯之名；
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: In my view, if your work succeeds you will enjoy Shen Bo's fame;
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: In my view, if merit is achieved and affairs succeed, you will surely enjoy the name of Shen Bo;

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 如或不立，將不免梁竇之跡矣。
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: if not, you will not escape the fate of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: If not, you will not escape the track of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Reading the histories, I see maternal relatives indulged and allowed to wield power and disorder the court: first they enjoy extraordinary glory, then suffer the consequences of holding positions beyond their station. This is what is meant by love proving sufficient to cause harm.
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Whenever I read the histories, I see maternal relatives invariably pampered and indulged, allowed to hold power and disorder the court; first they enjoy glory surpassing their age, then incur the burden of riding when unfit; this is what is meant by love being sufficient to cause harm.

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: I have often resented that successive rulers did not fully master the means of preventing incipient trouble while preserving favor to the end. Why not establish these relatives with a territorial fief and let their descendants inherit the vassal state, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing incipient trouble and preserving favor to the end; why not establish them with a territorial fief and let the vassal states be inherited in succession, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 如此則永保南面之尊，復何黜辱之憂乎！
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Then they would forever preserve honor facing south, with no fear of dismissal or disgrace!
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Then they would forever preserve the honor of facing south; what worry of dismissal and disgrace!

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 竇武、何進好善虛己。
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and humbled themselves.
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and emptied themselves.

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Worthy men rallied to them; although eunuchs brought them into peril, the realm lamented them because they could nonetheless conduct themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Worthy men gave them their hearts; although they were endangered by eunuch minions, the realm lamented them, because they were still able to conduct themselves without arrogance and took thought for the state at the cost of their lives.

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 方今四海有倒懸之急，中夏逋僭逆之寇，家有漉血之怨，人有復仇之憾，甯得安枕逍遙，雅談卒歲邪！
completeEnclosingParagraphs.en: Now the realm hangs inverted, rebels roam China, families bear blood-soaked grievances and men thirst for vengeance; how can one rest at ease and talk elegantly through the year!
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Now the four seas have the urgency of the inverted hanging; within China flee usurping rebels; families bear blood-soaked grievances and men the regret of vengeance; how can one rest on pillows at ease, discoursing elegantly through the year!

completeEnclosingParagraphs.zh: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！

With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!
completeEnclosingParagraphs.literal: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received the former emperor's appointment among the generals; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow powerful enemies; therefore from recent times until now, crossing weapons and meeting blades, one season for farming and three for war, yet the troops are not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy fears us more each day and our territory grows daily; how much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!
